chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Not being in need of putting forth an excuse is more noble than putting forth a true excuse.

key_terms.أَعَزُّ: More noble or higher in status
key_terms.الِاسْتِغْنَاءُ: Self-sufficiency or not being in need

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between having no excuse and having a true excuse according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates the spiritual and social status of 'self-sufficiency' (al-istighna') over mere factual accuracy, suggesting that a person who needs no justification possesses greater dignity than one who must truthfully explain their shortcomings. This reflects the Shia emphasis on inner integrity and high moral standing, where the absence of fault is superior to the presence of a valid defense. It serves as a practical guide for cultivating a character so upright that external validation becomes unnecessary.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 329. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Not to be in need of putting forth an excuse is better than putting forth a true excuse. [1]
